# Yitao Xu

> Yitao Xu is a Computer Science PhD student at George Mason University, advised by Dr. Ziyu Yao. Yitao Xu's research focuses on mechanistic interpretability, explainable AI, trustworthy large language models, and AI safety.

This file describes the Yitao Xu at George Mason University (advised by Dr. Ziyu Yao, member of George Mason NLP), whose homepage is https://nico21yt.github.io/. Other researchers share the name Yitao Xu; publications and profiles listed here belong to this person only.

## About

- Current position: PhD student in Computer Science, George Mason University (Fairfax, VA, USA), since Fall 2026
- Advisor: Dr. Ziyu Yao (https://ziyuyao.org/)
- Lab: George Mason NLP (https://nlp.cs.gmu.edu/) and Ziyu Yao's research group (https://littleyuyu.github.io/group/)
- Previous education: M.S. from Georgia Institute of Technology (Georgia Tech); B.Sc. from the University of Liverpool
- Research interests: mechanistic interpretability, explainable AI, trustworthy large language models, AI safety
- Contact: yxu30@gmu.edu

## Publications

- [The Illusion of Specialization: Unveiling the Domain-Invariant "Standing Committee" in Mixture-of-Experts Models](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.665/): ACL 2026 (Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 1: Long Papers). Authors: Yan Wang, Yitao Xu, Nanhan Shen, Jinyan Su, Jimin Huang, Zining Zhu. Yan Wang, Yitao Xu, and Nanhan Shen are co-first authors. Introduces CommitteeAudit and shows that routing in Mixture-of-Experts models is dominated by a domain-invariant "Standing Committee" of experts, challenging the assumption of strong domain specialization. DOI: 10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.665. PDF: https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.665.pdf
